join_order.notes: Resolve 2-3 lt_ids via memmem over 18 link_type rows; iterate movie_link rowids per lt_id using movie_link__link_type_id CSR (~3k-6k rows total)
For each ml row, dereference title.kind_id[t1_id-1]; reject if != tv_kind_id
Direct lookup title.kind_id[t2_id-1] AND title.production_year[t2_id-1]; year=2007 very strict
Walk mc rows for t1_id; require company_id in nl bitset; capture cn1.name for MIN
Need at least one mc row for t2; capture all company names for cn2 MIN

join_order.build: mi_idx1: movie_info_idx for t1_id where info_type_id==rating_id
mi_idx2: movie_info_idx for t2_id where info_type_id==rating_id AND info<'3.0' (lex)
join_order.notes: Lex compare via memcmp prefix; capture info for MIN(second_rating)

data_structures.cn1_nl_bitset: bitset(234998) of company_name ids with country_code=='[nl]'
data_structures.lt_ids_set: small int32 array (size 2-3) of matching link_type ids
data_structures.lt_id_to_text: per-lt_id pointer/length into link_type/link dat for MIN tracking (not needed - lt projection not in output)
data_structures.cn1_id_to_name: lazy lookup via company_name/name.{off,dat} on hit
data_structures.title_kind_id: raw int16 column - direct addressing by id-1
data_structures.title_production_year: raw int32 column - direct addressing by id-1
data_structures.min_aggregator: six string MIN trackers (compare via memcmp; store {len,offset}); finalize materializes from .dat

parallelism.strategy: morsel_driven over movie_link rowids matched by lt_ids
parallelism.notes: Total drive set is ~3k-6k ml rows; partition by ranges of CSR rowids. Per-thread local MIN trackers, merged at end. Small workload but partitioning OK for L3 friendliness.

indexes.purpose: drive ml rows by matching lt_ids
